statement: Independently constructed breakers that each transition from closed to open to half-open reach the same numeric generation.

After sequential replacement of a TwoStep receiver with a separate closed breaker in the same numeric generation, a retained false report can call the replacement's ReadyToTrip with one failure and no admissions.
After sequential replacement with a closed breaker in a different numeric generation, a retained false report does not reach that breaker's ReadyToTrip.
An old TwoStep callback can close a replacement half-open breaker with MaxRequests=1 when the two breaker generation numbers match.
After a foreign callback closes the target, the target's previously admitted half-open failure is ignored as stale.
A retained TwoStep callback that already reported to a replacement can report to its original breaker after the receiver is restored, if the original generation is still current.
One late half-open success with a matching generation and zero prior successes leaves a breaker with MaxRequests=2 half-open.
A State caller can propagate an Open-to-HalfOpen notification panic even though the transition is already committed.
Retrying State after an Open-to-HalfOpen notification panic does not replay that transition's notification.
ReadyToTrip calling runtime.Goexit during a closed Execute leaves its first counted failure in place without a fallback charge.
If recover returns nil for panic(nil) raised by an admitted request, Execute returns its zero result pair without submitting an outcome.
If recover returns nil for panic(nil) raised by the classifier, Execute returns its zero result pair without submitting an outcome.
A matching Execute fallback following a ReadyToTrip panic only charges a second failure if its generation still matches after state resolution.
A stale completion can invoke an expiry notification whose panic prevents the generation comparison from running.
If a half-open failure's reopening notification panics after the new timeout expires, Execute fallback can advance the breaker to half-open again.
For an old success aimed at an open replacement, unchanged counts alone cannot establish that the generation guard dropped the result because onSuccess has no open arm.
Time for deciding open expiry in a completion is sampled after acquiring the breaker mutex.
A half-open Execute worker whose waiter departed may report a matching success without closing if that report falls short of the threshold.
